questions.q: Why does this lesson say 'the system should be fast' fails as a real nonfunctional requirement?
options: Because performance is a functional requirement, not a nonfunctional one
Because it isn't measurable — nobody can test whether it's been met without a specific, checkable target
Because Salesforce does not allow performance-related requirements
Because speed only matters for the Dealer Portal, not the rest of the system
questions.explain: A real NFR needs a specific, checkable target; a vague aspiration like 'should be fast' can't actually be tested against, which is why every LTV Global NFR in this lesson has a concrete target attached.

questions.q: Which NFR in this lesson formalizes a design decision already made in Lesson 14, rather than introducing something new?
options: The scale NFR for 10,000 users
The availability NFR for portal business hours
The integration tolerance NFR, allowing Salesforce's financial visibility to lag LedgerPoint by up to one business day
The identity/SSO NFR
questions.explain: The integration tolerance NFR documents the batch tolerance window Lesson 14 already designed around for LedgerPoint — it's a formalization of an existing design fact, not a new decision.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say the integration tolerance NFR is especially important to write down explicitly before go-live?
options: Because without it, a finance user noticing the expected AR lag could become a production support escalation instead of confirmed, expected behavior
Because LedgerPoint requires written NFRs as a technical prerequisite for batch processing
Because it is the only NFR that affects EMEA specifically
Because it replaces the need for the reconciliation step in Lesson 14
questions.explain: Writing the tolerance down as an agreed requirement converts a known design fact into a shared expectation stakeholders signed off on, preventing it from surfacing as a surprise incident after go-live.

questions.q: How does this lesson say the performance NFR should actually be validated before go-live?
options: Through functional testing with a handful of sample records only
Through load testing against realistic peak-order volume, not just a small functional test dataset
By asking the Parts & Aftermarket VP to approve it without testing
Performance NFRs cannot be validated before go-live under any circumstances
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly ties performance NFR validation to load testing at realistic peak volume, contrasting it with the kind of small-sandbox testing that misses Large Data Volume problems until production.

questions.q: Which NFR in this lesson directly reflects Lesson 12's design, requiring that MFA enforcement be independently confirmed rather than assumed?
options: The scale NFR
The data residency NFR
The identity NFR for workforce SSO
The availability NFR
questions.explain: The identity NFR formalizes Lesson 12's point that Salesforce's MFA requirement doesn't independently fire during SSO, so Okta-side MFA enforcement must be explicitly confirmed, not assumed, as a checkable requirement.
